transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

No matter how much I rest, I feel completely drained and can’t keep up or focus at work anymore. It's gotten to the point where I'm constantly falling behind on my shifts at the clinic, and I just feel overwhelmed.
Over the past two weeks or longer, have you also been feeling down or losing interest in things you usually enjoy, or is it mainly the exhaustion and feeling overwhelmed?

It’s definitely both, and it's actually been going on for over a year now. I wake up every morning with this heavy, sinking feeling like a dark cloud is sitting on my chest, and I've completely lost interest in things I used to love like jogging or my Raspberry Pi projects. Most days I just end up staring at my workbench or scrolling on my phone, feeling totally hopeless.
Have you had any thoughts that life is not worth living, or thoughts of hurting yourself?

On my worst days, I catch myself thinking it would be easier if I just didn't wake up. I've even pictured driving my car off the highway on the way home a couple of times. But I don't have any actual plans, and I've never done anything to act on it.
Have you ever had a similar episode of depression before this one, or is this the first time you’ve felt this way for so long?

No, I’ve never felt this way before—this is the first time I’ve ever experienced an episode of depression like this. These hopeless, drained feelings started about a year to a year and a half ago, building up as my work stress and evening classes got more intense. Before all of this, I was always able to keep up and handle my schedule.
Have these low mood and loss of interest symptoms been present most of the day, nearly every day for at least two weeks at a time, or do they come and go?

They don't really come and go; it has been a constant, heavy presence almost every single day, most of the day, for over a year now. Aside from a few brief stretches where I felt completely numb rather than actively sad, that dark cloud and loss of interest have been there the entire time.
Have you ever had a period of at least several days where you felt unusually energized or euphoric, needed much less sleep, talked more than usual, or did things that were out of character for you?

No, I’ve never experienced anything like that at all. In fact, it’s been the exact opposite for me—I just feel constantly exhausted, drained, and incredibly low. I've never had periods of high energy or felt like I didn't need to sleep.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep, appetite, or weight during this time, such as sleeping much more or less than usual, eating less or more, or losing or gaining weight?

Yes, both have been really bad. I lie in bed for hours with my mind spinning about work, then wake up at 3 or 4 AM and can't fall back asleep. My appetite has also dropped so much that I just push food around and throw it away, and my coworkers have even noticed my scrubs are hanging off me from losing weight.
Did these symptoms start within about a month of a specific stressful or traumatic event, and have they mainly been tied to that stressor?

No, it wasn't a sudden change within a single month of one specific event. It built up gradually over almost two years, starting a few months after our clinic's electronic record upgrade and when I began my evening classes. It just steadily got worse as the staffing shortages and extra shifts piled on.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 months during this time when you felt back to your usual self, or have the symptoms been present most days without a break for over a year?

No, I haven't had any breaks where I felt like my usual self over these past two years. Even during a brief stretch last summer when my mood lifted slightly and I felt more numb than sad, I was still hearing that voice and feeling like the charting system was targeting me. I just haven't felt normal at all.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 months during this time when you felt back to your usual self, or has the low mood been present most days without a clear break for over a year?

No, I haven't had any clear two-month breaks where I felt back to my usual self. This low, drained feeling has been present for over a year now, steadily getting worse over the past year and a bit. Even during brief moments when I wasn't feeling outright sad, I just felt numb rather than normal.
Have you ever had a period of at least several days when you felt unusually energetic or irritable, needed much less sleep, talked more than usual, or became more active than normal?

No, I have never experienced periods of feeling unusually energetic, hyperactive, or needing less sleep. It has mostly been the exact opposite for me, where I just feel completely drained and slow all the time.

Have your low mood and loss of interest been present most of the time for at least 2 years, with only brief periods of feeling better, or have you had distinct episodes with clear return to normal in between?

Yes, the low mood and loss of interest have been present for most of the nearly two years since all of this started. I haven't had any clear returns to normal; at best, there were just a few brief stretches where I felt a bit numb rather than outright sad, but the heavy, hopeless feeling has been pretty constant.

Have you ever had a period of at least 2 months during these past two years when you felt back to your usual self, or have the low mood and loss of interest been present most days without a clear break?

No, I definitely haven't had any period of two months where I felt back to my usual self. The low mood and lack of interest have been present almost constantly for most of these past two years, with only a few brief times where I felt numb rather than sad, but never actually normal.

Have your low mood and loss of interest been present most days for at least 2 years without a long break, or have they come in distinct episodes with periods of feeling completely back to normal in between?

They have been present most days for nearly two years without any real break or return to normal. At best, there was a brief stretch last summer where my mood lifted slightly and I felt more numb than outright sad, but otherwise, this heavy, hopeless feeling has been a constant presence. I've definitely not had any distinct episodes where I felt completely back to my usual self.
Have these symptoms been present most of the day, nearly every day for at least 2 years, or did they start and end as a single episode lasting at least 2 weeks?

No, it definitely hasn't been a single short episode. These symptoms have been building and present nearly every day for almost two years, starting around the time of the clinic's record system change and my evening classes. That hopeless, drained feeling has been there for the vast majority of this two-year period.
During this time, have you ever had a stretch of at least 2 months when you felt back to your usual self, or has the low mood been present most days for 2 years or more without a clear break?

No, I haven't had any break like that where I felt back to my usual self at all. This low, hopeless feeling has been present almost constantly for most of the nearly two years this has been going on. Aside from a few brief periods where I just felt numb rather than outright sad, I have never felt normal or healthy.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 months during the past two years when you felt back to your usual self, or has the low mood been present most days without a clear break?

No, I haven't had a clear break of two months where I felt back to my usual self. The low, hopeless feeling has been present for most of the past two years, with only a few brief stretches where I felt numb rather than outright sad. Even during those times, I never felt truly normal.

Have your symptoms been present most of the time for at least 2 years without a period of feeling back to your usual self, or did they come in a single episode that lasted at least 2 weeks and then improve?

They have definitely been present for almost two years now, rather than being a single short episode. Aside from a few brief stretches where I felt numb instead of completely sad, I've had that hopeless, drained feeling and loss of interest for most of those two years.
During these low periods, have you ever heard voices, seen things others couldn’t, or felt strongly that people or events were trying to harm or control you?

Yes, I pretty often hear a low male voice behind me saying things like "you're screwing this up again," and I've been convinced the new charting system was designed specifically to track my mistakes and get my license pulled. These experiences became much worse and more frequent around the same time I started feeling constantly low and depressed.
Have you ever had times when the voices or suspicious beliefs were present even when your depression was not severe, or do they only happen during your low mood periods?

Yes, actually. Late last summer there was a stretch where my mood lifted slightly and I wasn't feeling quite as depressed, but I still heard that male voice criticizing me. Even during those weeks, I remained convinced that the charting system was tracking my mistakes.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when the voices or suspicious beliefs were present even though you were not feeling depressed or low at all?

Yes, late last summer there was a stretch of a few weeks where my mood lifted and I didn't feel quite as depressed. But even during those weeks, I still heard that male voice criticizing me and remained completely convinced the charting system was tracking my mistakes.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when the voices or suspicious beliefs were present even though you were not feeling depressed or low at all?

Yes, late last summer there was a stretch of about three weeks where my mood lifted and I wasn't feeling depressed. Even though my mood felt okay during those weeks, I still heard that male voice criticizing me and remained convinced the charting system was tracking my mistakes.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when you were hearing voices or had suspicious beliefs even though you were not depressed or low at all?

Yes, that did happen late last summer during a stretch of a few weeks when my mood had lifted and I wasn't feeling quite as down. Even though I wasn't feeling depressed then, I still heard that male voice telling me I was dangerous and remained convinced the charting system was tracking me.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when you were hearing voices or had suspicious beliefs even though you were not depressed or low at all?

Yes, late last summer there was a stretch of about three weeks where my mood lifted and I wasn't feeling particularly depressed. Even during those weeks, I still heard that low male voice calling me dangerous and remained convinced the charting system was tracking my mistakes.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when you were hearing voices or strongly suspicious even though you were not depressed or low at all?

Yes, that definitely happened late last summer during a stretch of about three weeks when my mood had lifted a bit and I wasn't feeling quite as down. Even though the heavy depression wasn't there during those weeks, I still kept hearing that male voice calling me dangerous and remained convinced the charting system was tracking my mistakes.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when you were hearing voices or strongly suspicious even though you were not depressed or low at all?

Yes, that's correct. Late last summer, there was a stretch of about three weeks where my mood lifted a bit and I wasn't feeling depressed, but I still heard that male voice calling me dangerous. Even during those weeks, I remained completely convinced that the charting system was tracking my mistakes.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when you were hearing voices or feeling suspicious while your mood was completely normal, with no depression at all?

Yes, late last summer there was a stretch of about three weeks where my mood had lifted and I wasn't feeling depressed at all. Even though my mood felt normal during those weeks, I still heard that male voice criticizing me and remained convinced the charting system was tracking my mistakes.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when you were hearing voices or feeling suspicious while your mood was completely normal, with no depression at all?

Yes, late last summer there was a stretch of about three weeks where my mood had lifted and I wasn't feeling depressed at all. Even though my mood felt normal then, I still heard that male voice criticizing me and remained convinced the charting system was tracking my mistakes.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when you were hearing voices or feeling suspicious while your mood was completely normal, with no depression at all?

Yes, late last summer there was a stretch of about three weeks where my mood lifted and I didn't feel depressed. Yet, during those weeks, I still heard that male voice criticizing me and was convinced the charting system was tracking my mistakes.
Have you ever had hallucinations or strong paranoid beliefs for at least 2 weeks when you were not depressed at all, and did those symptoms ever continue for about 2 weeks after your mood improved?

Yes, that's exactly what happened late last summer when my mood lifted a bit and I wasn't feeling depressed. Even though my mood had improved, I still heard that male voice calling me dangerous and remained convinced the charting system was tracking me for about three weeks.
